output.summary: KEP-1040 replaces the existing max-in-flight request handler in the apiserver with Priority and Fairness: each request is categorized into a priority level and a queue, with per-level concurrency pools, borrowing of unused concurrency, and even fairness among queues. The KEP is marked implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale:
The existing max-in-flight limits (mutating and readonly only) cannot stop one category of requests from crowding out others, and the two independent limits are not work-conserving. The design classifies requests into priority levels and queues so self-maintenance, controllers, and tenants can be protected from overload. Its stated goal priority order is overload protection, then fairness, then throughput.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Keep the existing max-in-flight limits for mutating and readonly requests
alternatives.why_not: The readonly/mutating split makes no other distinctions, so one subset of load can crowd out others, and the two limits are not work-conserving.
Non-goal: 'This KEP will not attempt auto-tuning the capacity limit(s).' Administrators configure each apiserver's limits instead.

alternatives.option: Coordinate across apiservers or with a load balancer
alternatives.why_not: Non-goal: 'No coordination between apiservers nor with a load balancer is attempted.' Each apiserver protects itself independently.

alternatives.option: Thread priority information through webhooks to avoid priority inversions
alternatives.why_not: Non-goal: the KEP instead asks the configuration to identify secondary requests and give them sufficiently high priority.

evidence.quote: each request is categorized to a priority level and a queue within that priority level; each priority level dispatches to its own concurrency pool
Apart from the distinction between mutating and readonly, no other distinctions are made among requests; consequently there can be undesirable scenarios
This KEP will not attempt auto-tuning the capacity limit(s). Instead the administrator will configure each apiserver's capacity limit(s)
Remove the feature gate, planned for 1.31 (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/121639)
